title: Gilgamesh

vessel.subject: Gilgamesh tradition
vessel.purpose: first MOBIUS benchmark: curate a historically layered story instance whose survival demonstrates impact beyond the lifetime of an author, ruler, scribe, or copy

truth_snapshot.claim: Surviving Gilgamesh literature exists in cuneiform clay-tablet traditions from ancient Mesopotamia.
Earlier Sumerian Gilgamesh poems precede later Akkadian epic forms.
The Standard Babylonian version is traditionally associated with Sin-leqi-unninni.
The historical status and exact biography of a real King Gilgamesh cannot simply be equated with the epic's literary character.
Mortality, friendship, kingship, loss, journeys, and enduring works are central story material.

lineage.primary_medium: cuneiform signs impressed on clay tablets
lineage.author_lineage: many earlier anonymous/traditional compositions; Standard Babylonian recension traditionally attributed to Sin-leqi-unninni
lineage.portrait_policy: no invented historical portrait; use artifact/scribal/material references unless a depiction is explicitly labeled as later interpretation
